    Pico link stress¶

    How reliably does a scope talk to its Picos, and how many Picos can one machine drive? This notebook measures the round trip of a call to every Pico on a scope as the call rate rises, the most the link does flat out, how fast a lost link comes back, and what a hung call or a broken job does to the scheduler that every recording uses.

    Analysis written by Claude (Anthropic); conceptualised and verified by Yatharth Bhasin.

    Protocol¶

    Acquisition: scripts/debug/pico_link_stress.py, create_exp() then start_acq_blocking(). No acquisition may run at the same time. The short run takes about 4 minutes with one Pico.

    Every Pico plugged into the scope is tested at once: the ones the scope mounted at start-up as they are, any other one connected directly by its port. Nothing else needs to be wired to them. Each call is one round trip through the production path (SerialMPDevice → raw REPL), sent from exp.schedule: it toggles the onboard LED, adds two random numbers and returns the sum with the board's uptime. The sum is checked.

    The steps, in order: a ramp of requested rates per Pico (1–50 calls/s); a burst of back-to-back calls; two drills per Pico (close and reconnect the port, then machine.reset() and wait for the board to come back); a job that raises inside exp.schedule; a job that blocks it for 10 s; and a call that never returns, which the recovery ladder has to clear (wait, Ctrl-C, soft reset, reconnect, hard reset). To map how the link scales, run it with one Pico plugged in, then another one alone, then both together.

    Running in Colab. Open this notebook with the Open in Colab button on its page. The next cell runs only in Colab: it installs what Colab lacks and asks for a .zip of your experiment folders.

    Data¶

    Runs are read with trappy-explorer's legacy reader, explorer.legacy.ExpExplorer. One row per run; n_picos is how many Picos the run tested.

exps = ExpExplorer.create_superset(DATA, extended_parse=True)
rich.get_console().quiet = False

ms = exps.df_events.query("type == 'measurement_stream'")
res = exps.df.assign(stream=exps.df.measureid.map(dict(zip(ms.measureid, ms.name))))

runs = pd.DataFrame([{"scope": d["metadata"]["name"].split("__")[0], "eid": eid,
                      "started": d["metadata"]["created"], "dir": exps.get_parent_dir(eid)}
                     for eid, d in exps.data.items()]).sort_values(["scope", "started"])
runs["run"] = runs.groupby("scope").cumcount() + 1
J = {r.eid: json.load(open(f"{r.dir}/pico_stress.json")) for r in runs.itertuples()}
runs["n_picos"] = runs.eid.map(lambda e: J[e].get("n_picos", len(J[e]["devices"])))
runs["devices"] = runs.eid.map(lambda e: ", ".join(J[e]["devices"]))
runs["end"] = runs.eid.map(lambda e: J[e]["end"])
runs = runs.join(res.groupby(["eid", "stream"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0), on="eid")

SCOPES = sorted(runs.scope.unique(), key=lambda s: (len(s), s))
COLORS = {s: PALETTE[i % len(PALETTE)] for i, s in enumerate(SCOPES)}
runs.set_index(["scope", "run"]).drop(columns="dir")

picos          8 rows   board, device, led_ok, mpy, port, uid
steps         80 rows   device, achieved_hz, errors, max_ms, n, ok, p50_ms, p99_ms, rate_hz, recoveries, step, timeouts, wrong

    The two streams hold one row per Pico (picos) and one row per Pico per step (steps). Each run folder also holds the files the analysis uses:

    • calls.csv: every call, with step, requested rate_hz, device, latency_ms, outcome (ok, timeout, error, wrong) and, from script 7e26f77 on, the board's uptime pico_ms.
    • events.csv: recoveries, drills and injected faults, one row each.
    • system.csv: once a second, the Pi's throttled flags and whether the scheduler thread is alive.
    • pico_stress.json: the run's summary, including drill times and the scheduler results.
    • kernel.log: kernel messages. It starts with the kernel's buffer, so it reaches back before the run.

    Copied! 
    def load_calls(r):
    c = pd.read_csv(f"{r.dir}/calls.csv")
    return c.assign(scope=r.scope, run=r.run, eid=r.eid, n_picos=r.n_picos)

calls = pd.concat([load_calls(r) for r in runs.itertuples()], ignore_index=True)
calls["failed"] = (calls.outcome != "ok") & (calls.call != "hang")   # the injected hang must time out
ramp = calls[calls.step == "ramp"].assign(rate_hz=lambda d: d.rate_hz.astype(float))
calls.groupby(["scope", "run", "device", "outcome"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0)

    Response time as the call rate rises¶

    Each line is one Pico in one run, through the ramp steps. Left: the 99th percentile of the round trip at each requested rate; a line that bends upward marks the rate at which calls start to queue. Right: the rate the calls actually ran at. exp.schedule checks for due jobs every 10 ms, so the achieved rate falls below the requested one as it nears 50 calls/s even on a healthy link. A step at a low rate has few calls, so its p99 is close to its single slowest call.

    In [7]:
    Copied! 
    def summarise(g):
    t = g.t_wall.sort_values()
    span = t.iloc[-1] - t.iloc[0]
    return pd.Series({"p50_ms": g.latency_ms.median(), "p99_ms": g.latency_ms.quantile(0.99),
                      "achieved_hz": (len(t) - 1) / span if span > 0 else np.nan,
                      "failed": g.failed.mean()})

rs = (ramp.groupby(["scope", "run", "n_picos", "device", "rate_hz"])[["t_wall", "latency_ms", "failed"]]
      .apply(summarise).reset_index())
rs["pico"] = rs.scope + " " + rs.device + " run " + rs.run.astype(str)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))
for ax, y, label in zip(axes, ["p99_ms", "achieved_hz"], ["p99 round trip (ms)", "achieved calls/s"]):
    sns.lineplot(rs, x="rate_hz", y=y, hue="scope", palette=COLORS, units="pico", estimator=None,
                 style="n_picos", markers=True, ax=ax)
    ax.set_xscale("log")
    plain_log(ax.xaxis)
    ax.set_xlabel("requested calls/s per Pico")
    ax.set_ylabel(label)
axes[1].set_yscale("log")
plain_log(axes[1].yaxis)
axes[0].get_legend().remove()
sns.move_legend(axes[1], "upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1))
fig.tight_layout()

    Round-trip times¶

    The distribution of the round trip of every good call in the ramp and the burst, on a log axis. A curve that rises steeply in one place means a steady link. A tail stretching to the right is calls that waited: for the USB bus, for the Pico, or for the scheduler.

    How many Picos can one machine drive?¶

    The phase space: rows are the number of Picos a run tested, columns the requested rate per Pico, pooled over every scope and run. Left: the 99th percentile round trip. Right: the fraction of calls that failed. A row needs runs with that many Picos plugged in; the cells where the colour changes are the limits of one machine. Below: the most calls per second the machine got through flat out (the burst), summed over its Picos, one point per run.

    Recovery¶

    How long each way back took, one point per Pico per run: closing and reconnecting the port, a machine.reset() until the board answers again, and a call that never returns until the ladder has the board answering again (the first step waits late_reply_s for a late reply before it acts). The table gives the same times and the ladder step that cleared each hung call.

    In [10]:
    Copied! 
    rec = []
for r in runs.itertuples():
    for dev, d in J[r.eid]["devices"].items():
        for x in d["drills"]:
            rec.append({"scope": r.scope, "run": r.run, "device": dev, "action": f"drill: {x['kind']}",
                        "seconds": x["ms"] / 1000, "ok": x["ok"], "by": "-"})
    for dev, h in J[r.eid].get("pico_hang", {}).items():
        rec.append({"scope": r.scope, "run": r.run, "device": dev, "action": "hung call",
                    "seconds": h["seconds"], "ok": h["recovered_by"] is not None,

    The scheduler¶

    Every recording runs its periodic jobs on exp.schedule, one thread. The run injects a job that raises and a job that sleeps for schedule_hang_s. The table shows, per run, whether the raise killed the thread, how many Pico calls ran after it, whether the boards still answered a direct call, how many calls ran once the thread was restarted, and the longest any Pico waited while the scheduler slept.

    USB and power¶

    The kernel log is searched for every USB port a Pico has used. pico_usb_drops_in_run counts the disconnects on those ports during the run; each machine.reset() drill causes exactly one, so any more is a Pico that dropped off the bus on its own. pico_usb_drops_in_log counts them over the whole log, which reaches back before the run. throttled lists every value of the Pi's throttled flags seen during the run; 0x0 means no under-voltage and no thermal throttling.

    In [12]:
    Copied! 
    KT = re.compile(r"^\[(\w{3} \w{3}\s+\d+ \d\d:\d\d:\d\d \d{4})\]")

def usb(r):
    lines = open(f"{r.dir}/kernel.log", errors="replace").read().splitlines()
    ports = {m.group(1) for l in lines if re.search(r"idVendor=2e8a|Board in FS mode", l)
             for m in [re.search(r"usb (\d+-[\d.]+):", l)] if m}
    drops = [pd.to_datetime(" ".join(KT.match(l).group(1).split()), format="%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y")
             for l in lines if KT.match(l) and "USB disconnect" in l
             and any(f"usb {p}:" in l for p in ports)]
    t0, t1 = pd.Timestamp(J[r.eid]["started"]).floor("s"), pd.Timestamp(J[r.eid]["finished"])
    sysl = pd.read_csv(f"{r.dir}/system.csv", dtype={"throttled": str})
    return {"scope": r.scope, "run": r.run,
            "kernel_log_from": " ".join(KT.match(lines[0]).group(1).split()) if lines else None,
            "pico_usb_drops_in_log": len(drops),
            "pico_usb_drops_in_run": sum(t0 <= t <= t1 for t in drops),
            "machine_reset_drills": sum(x["kind"] == "machine_reset" for d in J[r.eid]["devices"].values()
                                        for x in d["drills"]),
            "throttled": " ".join(sorted(sysl.throttled.dropna().unique())) or "not read"}

usbt = pd.DataFrame([usb(r) for r in runs.itertuples()]).set_index(["scope", "run"])
usbt

    Copied! 
    def pico_row(r, dev, d):
    g = calls[(calls.eid == r.eid) & (calls.device == dev)]
    rg, bg = g[g.step == "ramp"], g[g.step == "burst"]
    drills = {x["kind"]: x for x in d["drills"]}
    hang = J[r.eid].get("pico_hang", {}).get(dev, {})
    u = usbt.loc[(r.scope, r.run)]
    return {"scope": r.scope, "run": r.run, "eid": r.eid, "n_picos": r.n_picos, "device": dev,
            "board": d["board"], "micropython": d["mpy"], "mounted_by_scope": not d["owned"],
            "calls": len(g), "failed": int(g.failed.sum()), "fatal": d["fatal"],
            "peak_hz": d["peak_hz"], "max_hz": max(J[r.eid]["attribs"]["ramp_hz"]),
            "ramp_p50_ms": rg.latency_ms.median(), "ramp_p99_ms": rg.latency_ms.quantile(0.99),
            "burst_calls_s": (len(bg) - 1) / (bg.t_wall.max() - bg.t_wall.min()) if len(bg) > 1 else None,
            "reconnect_s": drills.get("reconnect", {}).get("ms", np.nan) / 1000,
            "reset_s": drills.get("machine_reset", {}).get("ms", np.nan) / 1000,
            "drills_ok": all(x["ok"] for x in d["drills"]),
            "hang_cleared_by": hang.get("recovered_by"), "hang_s": hang.get("seconds"),
            "schedule_thread_died": sch.loc[(r.scope, r.run, dev), "thread_died"],
            "block_wait_s": sch.loc[(r.scope, r.run, dev), "longest_wait_s"],
            "unexpected_usb_drops": u.pico_usb_drops_in_run - u.machine_reset_drills,
            "throttled": u.throttled}

    8 rows × 21 columns

    About the data shown here (first run, 2026-11-15). Each scope had one Pico plugged in, so the phase space has a single row until runs with more Picos are added. The Picos do not all run the same firmware: M1–M4 MicroPython 1.24.1 (board names pico_m1–pico_m4), M5 1.23.0, M6–M8 1.24.0 with the generic board name picodev; M5's calls are about 1 ms faster than the rest. M6's kernel log starts at 14:35:59, a minute before its run: the Pi had just booted. Every kernel log also shows a keyboard and mouse hub reconnecting many times; those are not Pico ports and are not counted.

    Acceptance¶

    Per Pico, per run:

    Criterion Level
    Any call timed out, errored or came back wrong, apart from the one injected hang FAIL
    The board could not be recovered (fatal) FAIL
    A reconnect or machine.reset() drill did not bring the board back FAIL
    The recovery ladder did not clear the injected hang FAIL
    A Pico dropped off USB other than in the reset drill FAIL
    The Pi reported under-voltage or throttling (throttled flags other than 0x0) FAIL
    A ramp step was not clean: p99 above p99_limit_ms, or a failure or recovery in it WARN

    The scheduler results are reported but not judged: they describe exp.schedule, which is the same code on every scope.
